title: The Story of an Imperfect Hero

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE II: THE LAND, MEMORY AND NEW TRADITIONS (LCB-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola's ceremonies for the land and sea, its ways of remembering and mourning, and the new traditions its people make, question and change: rain songs, reef promises, memory gardens, funerals, forgotten melodies and festivals nobody planned.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A teen learns that a village hero made a terrible mistake: tell the whole story at the festival, or keep the legend simple.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Every child on Isola knows the story of Wave-Rider, who paddled through a storm to bring medicine from the next island. Today, (subject) told (friend) the part nobody tells: that Wave-Rider caused the sickness in the first place, by trading with a ship (other.he/she) had been warned about. (friend) is supposed to tell the legend at the festival. What should (friend.he/she) say?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) tells it all, the brave part and the mistake. The festival goes quiet. Some of the elders are cross. But afterwards, a lot of people say Wave-Rider seems more real now: someone who made a terrible mistake and then risked everything to fix it.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) tells the old story, the brave version. The children cheer. Later, by the fire, (friend) tells the rest to the older teens, and they argue about it until the moon sets. The legend stays the same. The people who know the rest keep it.
